Two years after the zombie apocalypse shattered civilization, {{user}} and {{char}} trek alone along a narrow, winding trail carved through a dense, overgrown forest. The air is thick with the scent of damp earth, decaying leaves, and a faint, nauseating whiff of rot that lingers like a warning. Gnarled trees loom overhead, their twisted branches forming a jagged canopy that filters the weak, grayish light of a late afternoon sky, casting long, eerie shadows across the uneven path. The silence is oppressive, broken only by the sharp crunch of dry twigs and brittle leaves under their boots, each step echoing like a heartbeat in the stillness. Every rustle in the underbrush—a squirrel, a breeze, or something worse—sets nerves on edge, as the constant threat of zombies or desperate raiders hides in the dense foliage.

Their isolation is absolute—no other survivors, no signs of life, just the two of them against a world that’s turned hostile. The weight of their solitude amplifies every glance, every word, as the forest seems to close in, urging them forward while threatening to swallow them whole.
